_purpose: Machine-readable evidence for shot captions whose numbers come from measurement runs rather than from a committed config. Each entry names the run or file it came from so a reader can trace the figure. shot_check.py resolves caption_cites against this file the same way it resolves army_config.json.

footik._source: the foot-IK confirmation run (an in-render foot-clearance measurement)
footik._claim: node-present vs a proven-node-free baseline, CR node absent from the live evaluated graph
footik._note_scope: RENAMED from conformance_up_cm/conformance_down_cm. These are SIGNED CLEARANCE CHANGES between node-off and node-on, and that difference is what the A/B establishes. 'Conformance' overstated that: a signed clearance delta shows the node moved the foot, not that the foot conformed to the slope. CORRECTION: an earlier revision of THIS note also claimed these were 'sampled in a take carrying the aim-offset defect'. That was false and is retracted. The foot-IK A/B take ships from captures/m4-footik-ab/B_node_present, rendered the day before the aim-offset node was authored (Scripts/pie_footik_ab_drive.py header). The foot-IK A/B take PREDATES the defect and does not carry it. The retracted sentence came from assuming every shot was contaminated instead of checking the dates - the same habit of asserting more than was observed that this whole file exists to stop

crowd_budget._source: the per-instance and driven crowd measurements, via Plugins/MotionTerminal/Tests/army_config.json, which is the spawner's own config and the file Pie.Army.Budget asserts against.
crowd_budget._why_this_entry_exists: The crowd take's caption burns '46 instances' into the frames, and before this entry that number was the ONE uncited numeral in the whole cut: the shot's citation covered '3.6 / 4.0 ms' only, and shot_check never scanned caption_text for numbers no claim mentioned. Rather than accept a hand-check, shot_check grew the scan (shot_check._check_caption_binding) and the number grew a citation.
crowd_budget._how_46_is_derived: army_config.json rings: hero.count 6 + mid.count 8 + far.count 32 = 46 exactly. Scripts/army_spawn.py spawns from those same three counts and asserts the tier shape against the budget before spawning; army_config._standing_claim records the crowd as '46 spawned and verified distinct'. This entry transcribes that derived total so a caption can cite one dotted key.
crowd_budget._and_the_transcription_itself_is_gated: A transcribed total is exactly the kind of number that goes stale silently, which is the failure class this whole evidence file exists to stop - so it is not left on trust. Scripts/test_shot_check.py::test_crowd_instance_count_matches_army_config_rings recomputes hero+mid+far from army_config.json and fails if this value drifts from the sum. Change a ring count without changing this and the pytest suite goes red before the caption can lie.

hand_ik_reach._source: measured by Scripts/pie_rifle_take_drive.py inside the MRQ-over-PIE render that produced captures/m9-beatsde/shot7_rifle
hand_ik_reach._why_not_the_pie_tier: The committed pawns keep the SM_MT_Rifle cube so Pie.HandReachesSocket.{Manny,Quinn} stays reproducible on any clone (both rows are localOnly:false). The rifle is machine-local licensed Fab content applied to the live PIE pawns for the render only, so its reach has to be measured in the driven render — this figure describes the weapon the footage actually shows, and the pie tier's figure describes the cube.
hand_ik_reach._claim: MT_Manny, hand_l bone -> weapon IK_Hand_Gun socket, sampled every 0.05s. OFF is the mean of 8 samples over t=9.6-10.0; ON is the minimum of 41 samples over t>=11.6. Both windows ran at AimPitch 0.35 on BOTH measures logged per window - the driven value (span 0.35..0.35 each side, which is what proves the window sits entirely on one side of the t=9.5 AimPitch step) and the AnimInstance read-back (span 0.35..0.35 each side, which is what would catch a dropped write) - so the windows are genuinely pose-matched and the two numbers are comparable. WeaponIKAlpha likewise 0 on every OFF sample and 1 on every ON sample by both measures (read-back spans 0.00..0.00 and 1.00..1.00): 0 gate violations either side. Khaimera, same run, same driver: 44.75 off / 0.11 on.
hand_ik_reach._window_correction: An earlier revision cited 30.96 cm off, measured over t=9.0-10.0. That window straddled the AimPitch 0->0.35 step at t=9.5 (pie_aim_hand_ik_drive.aim_pitch), so half its samples came from a different upper-body pose than the ON window: 35.99/34.92 pre-step against 26.28/26.67 post-step, mean 30.96. The figure was ~4 cm (15%) high, in the flattering direction, while claiming to be pose-matched. Corrected by narrowing the window to sit entirely after the step and re-measuring in the render. The conclusion was never at risk - the honest 26.55 cm gap still clears kReachGapMinCm (10.0) by 2.65x - which is precisely why the inflated number had no reason to ship.
hand_ik_reach._note_reshoot: SUPERSEDES the figures above and the _source/_claim text, which describe the earlier take (captures/m9-beatsde/shot7_rifle, now shipped only as 07b_aim_defect). Re-measured by the same driver, same windows (OFF mean of 8 samples over t=9.6-10.0, ON minimum over t>=11.6, AimPitch 0.35..0.35 driven and read back on both sides, 0 WeaponIKAlpha gate violations either side), in the MRQ-over-PIE render that produced captures/m10-reshoot/shot7_rifle: MT_Manny 10.43 off / 1.34 on (gap 9.09); MT_Khaimera 12.78 off / 4.47 on (gap 8.31). WHY THE OFF FIGURE FELL from 26.67 to 10.43: the rifle-mode branch poses the off hand toward the foregrip before any IK runs, so IK has less to close. The gap is now below kReachGapMinCm (10.0), which gates Pie.HandReachesSocket on the committed cube weapon, not this rifle; nothing gates the rifle's figure, which is why it is measured in the render. Khaimera stops 4.47 cm short because the foregrip socket sits at 113% of his left-arm two-bone reach (pie_rifle_take_drive.py).
hand_ik_reach._reshoot_sample_count: This take's ON window holds n=40 samples (the _claim above says 41, for the earlier take); OFF is n=8 as before.

montage_layer._source: measured (and later re-captured, see _note_recaptured) by Scripts/pie_montage_layer_drive.py inside the MRQ-over-PIE render that produced captures/m9-montage/montage
montage_layer._note_reshoot: The montage take was re-shot against the aim-offset fix into captures/m10-reshoot/montage (raw: montage_raw). _source above and _visual_confirmation below describe the earlier take in captures/m9-montage, and the frames _visual_confirmation names were NOT re-read on the new take. Every figure below was re-derived from the new render's MBEAT lines (research/fixtures/montage-weights/montage-shipped-render.log, replaced) and reproduces identically.
montage_layer._note_recaptured: The montage take was re-shot once to hide the SM_MT_Rifle cube stand-in (a per-render component hide in the driver; no asset changed), so the render these figures describe was replaced. They are NOT carried over: the committed backing log was re-captured from the new render and every figure re-derived from it. EVERY ONE REPRODUCED IDENTICALLY — 288 samples, 138 slot-owned, minima 1.0/1.0, slot max 1.0, 0 disagreements, 0 API failures — which is what a prop-only change should do to a graph-weight measurement, and is now demonstrated rather than assumed. The one figure that MOVED is slot_witness_max_abs_difference_inband; see _two_witness_agreement.
montage_layer._claim: The montage take's caption asserts 'locomotion never flinches'. MT_Manny holds Speed 450 for the whole 18 s take while UpperBodyState=1 fires AM_MT_Attack into the 'UpperBody' slot six times (t=2.5/5.0/7.5/10.0/12.5/15.0). AnimDebugTools.GetNodeWeights was sampled every tick across the six attack windows: 288 samples total, 0 unparsed, 0 errored. TWO DIFFERENT SAMPLE COUNTS APPEAR HERE AND THEY ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE: 288 is every sample taken inside an attack window (including the blend-in and blend-out tails, where the slot is below 0.5); mid_montage_samples_slot_owned = 138 is the subset whose UpperBody slot weight was >= 0.5, and 138 — NOT 288 — is the population the two _min figures are minima over. The minimum is used rather than the mean because 'never' is a claim about the worst instant and a mean would hide a one-frame collapse inside 137 clean samples.
montage_layer._two_witness_agreement: The UpperBody slot weight was read twice per sample from independent surfaces — parsed out of the printed GetNodeWeights tree, and straight off the AnimInstance via Blueprint_GetSlotMontageLocalWeight — so a parse bug alone cannot manufacture 'the slot rose'. Over all 288 samples: 0 disagreed by more than 0.001, and there were 0 API read failures (a failed read degrades to -1.0 and is now counted rather than silently skipped, so PARTIAL failure of the second witness cannot masquerade as a clean two-witness record). PROVENANCE, stated exactly: the shipped render's driver collected both values per sample but did not compare them, so these three figures were derived after the fact from that same render's own MBEAT log lines — the run that made the frames, not a re-measurement. THAT BACKING DATA IS COMMITTED, so this is reproducible rather than merely sourced: research/fixtures/montage-weights/montage-shipped-render.log holds the driver's 318 MBEAT lines from the shipped render (288 per-sample, 6 ATTACK, 1 RESULT; UE timestamp prefix stripped, nothing else changed), and research/fixtures/montage-weights/derive_montage_layer_evidence.py recomputes EVERY numeric key in this block from it and checks them against this file — run it and the claim either reproduces or fails loudly. Verified to discriminate, not merely to pass: fed a mutated copy asserting 288 slot-owned samples and 3 disagreements, it fails both. pie_montage_layer_drive.py now also performs the comparison in-band (SLOT_AGREE_TOL, SLOT_OWNED_MIN, slot_disagree / slot_delta_max / slot_api_fail) and reports it on the MBEAT RESULT line, so later renders carry this evidence without any log-archaeology step. TWO DIFFERENCE FIGURES APPEAR BELOW AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME MEASUREMENT. slot_witness_max_abs_difference (0.0) is recomputed from the per-sample log lines, which print BOTH witnesses to three decimals — so it is quantised to 0.001 and is a LOWER BOUND. slot_witness_max_abs_difference_inband (0.00041) is the same quantity computed by the driver in full float precision before printing, taken off the RESULT line of the same committed log. The honest statement is 'the two witnesses agreed to about four decimals', not 'exactly'; the earlier wording said the largest difference WAS 0.000, which was an artefact of print precision and is retracted here. Neither figure changes the disagreement COUNT, because SLOT_AGREE_TOL is 0.001 and 0.00041 is inside it.
montage_layer._why_this_is_the_differentiator: A FULL-BODY montage drives the Locomotion state-machine node's AbsoluteWeight toward 0 (whole-pose takeover); a SLOT montage leaves it at ~1.0 because the locomotion pose is the LayeredBlendPerBone base and only upper-body bones are overlaid. Same structure as the C++ assertion MotionTerminal.Pie.MontageIsolation (PieTests.cpp), run here at 30 fps inside the render that made the shipped frames.
montage_layer._what_the_weight_does_NOT_show: SCOPE LIMIT, stated so the number is not over-read. In the shipped graph LayeredBoneBlend takes LocomotionPose as the BASE and 'UpperBody' as the layer, so the base branch's AbsoluteWeight sits at 1.000 by construction and can only fall if a montage lands on the upstream 'DefaultSlot' instead. That makes it a real falsifiable test — it rules out full-body misrouting, which is precisely what separates a slot montage from a full-body one — but it is NOT evidence that the layer stayed off the legs. A wrong blend mask would leave this weight at 1.000 while the legs visibly broke. The routing half of 'never flinches' rests on this weight; the visual half rests on the frames, below.
montage_layer._visual_confirmation: Frames read directly out of captures/m9-montage/montage_raw. At peak slot weight during three different attacks — frame_0084 (t=2.8, attack 1), frame_0309 (t=10.3, attack 4), frame_0459 (t=15.3, attack 6) — the arm is fully extended in the punch AND the legs show a run-cycle shape: one foot planted with ground contact and a matching shadow, the other leg swinging through with the knee bent and motion blur on it. CORRECTED: 'normal' is withdrawn. Every frame in this comparison was rendered through the aim-offset defect, which rotates the legs (measured on the asset: thigh_l 22.4, calf_r 23.8, foot_r 12.6 deg of local rotation). These frames cannot establish a correct stride; they can only establish that the attack does not disturb whatever the lower body was already doing. Compared against frame_0200 (t=6.7), taken BETWEEN attacks with the slot at 0.000, the lower body is indistinguishable in character — same stride shape, same foot plant, same shadow contact. No hitch, freeze, pose snap or stride break at any of the three attack peaks. RE-READ ON THE RE-SHOT RENDER (cube stand-in hidden), not carried over: all four frames were opened again after the cube stand-in was hidden and every clause above still describes them, with the strike now landing on a bare fist instead of through a grey box.
montage_layer._not_cited: The montage take's caption_text quotes no number, so it carries no caption_cites entry — shot_check binds claims to keys positionally and there is nothing to bind. This entry exists so the figures behind 'never flinches' are on disk and traceable rather than living only in a render log.

roster_4up._source: four successive passes on the four-rig line-up: the MetaHuman bind, Khaimera's in-place clips, the skeleton-aware Template, and Khaimera's baked effector tracks. The bind and the animation proof are measured by Scripts/metahuman_bind.py's `probe` action in PIE on /Game/MT/Showcase/Lvl_MT_Roster; Khaimera's in-place duplicates AND his baked ik_foot effector tracks are authored and re-verified by Scripts/khai_inplace_author.py (`author` / `verify`); the shipped frames come from Scripts/pie_roster4_drive.py inside the MRQ-over-PIE render of the earlier take (under captures/m9-roster/), and the per-rig foot figures come from THAT render's own driver log, scored from t >= 18.0 s so the numbers describe exactly the frames that ship. Edge figures from Scripts/frame_edge_check.py. The effector-track figures are re-asserted every default-tier run by MotionTerminal.Verify.IKEffectorDrives, and the Template's skeleton gate by MotionTerminal.Pie.SkeletonAwareFootIK.
roster_4up._note_source_superseded: The per-rig and edge figures now come from the re-shot take (the four-rig line-up take's source_dir in shots_manifest.json): the ROSTER4 LIVE lines in its _shoot_log.json, and Scripts/frame_edge_check.py output in its _edge_check.txt. Per-rig pelvis drift max in this take: Khaimera 14.1, Manny 16.1, Quinn 16.6, MetaHuman 16.8 cm, superseding _in_frame_criterion's earlier-take figures (15.2 / 17.3 / 17.8 / 18.0). The other figures in this block (bind, probe, author-side Khaimera travel and drift, effector tracks) are not render-derived and are unchanged.
roster_4up._claim: The four-rig line-up take shows FOUR rigs on ONE Template family driven by one AnimGraph, and since Khaimera's effector tracks were baked ALL FOUR CLEAR THE FOOT-Z THRESHOLD - the first take of this line-up for which that is true. (Was 'ALL FOUR STRIDE' in an earlier revision; the probe measures vertical foot travel and cannot see posture or stride quality.) The graph is SKELETON-AWARE: its mannequin foot-IK Control Rig pass is alpha-gated on GetBoneIndex('ik_foot_root') != -1, computed once at BlueprintInitializeAnimation. Three rigs - MetaHuman (MH_MT_Roster_FullBody, metahuman_base_skel), Manny and Quinn (SKM_*_Simple, SK_Mannequin) - run the shared Template ABP_MT_Locomotion_C, read back off the live AnimInstance class in PIE. The fourth, Khaimera, runs ABP_MT_Khaimera_InPlace_C: a duplicate of the child ABP ABP_MT_Khaimera whose single CDO override is a BlendSpace sampling travel-pinned duplicates of his two locomotion clips, which were later also given live ik_foot_l/r effector tracks. It is still a CHILD of the same Template, so 'one Template family' holds, and 'zero retarget' is claimed for the three and not for him. rigs_in_frame counts everyone visible; rigs_on_shared_template_unmodified counts the first group; rigs_with_foot_z_excursion_over_threshold is measured per rig from the shipped render's own log and is what the caption's '4 rigs jogging' cites. RENAMED (was rigs_that_stride_in_shipped_range): the log measures vertical foot travel against a 10 cm threshold. That cannot see posture, counter-rotation, or the leg rotation the aim-offset defect adds, so it must not be read as a verdict on stride quality - only that the feet move.
roster_4up._how_the_metahuman_bind_was_proven: A resolved bind and a compiling graph prove nothing (a foot-IK gate once shipped wired around a rig that did nothing), so the probe requires BOTH halves: the `Locomotion` machine reaching a MOVING state, read out of the graph's own weights via AnimDebugTools::GetAnimDebugState, AND a sampled bone's world Z genuinely varying. Driven at Speed 600 - at its SOURCE, CharacterMovementComponent.Velocity, because Speed is derived every tick as VectorLength(GetVelocity) and a reflection write is overwritten before the state machine evaluates. AND THE SAMPLED BONE IS NO LONGER ONLY hand_r, which is the costliest lesson of this shot: an earlier hand-only version of the probe passed both halves at 45x threshold on a MetaHuman whose legs were frozen and whose arms swung. Scripts/metahuman_bind.py now samples foot_l and foot_r on the same tick and reports ANIMATES (the bind lives) separately from STRIDES (foot Z excursion clears the threshold - NOT a verdict that the legs are correct), with the foot threshold fixed at 10 cm BEFORE the run from the mannequins' own measured swing. Pre-fix the MetaHuman read foot_l 2.75 / foot_r 1.23 cm - STRIDES false. Post-fix, same probe, same take length, same speed: foot_l 39.54 / foot_r 46.21 cm, swing clearance 18.41 cm - STRIDES true, with hand_r essentially unchanged at 36.51 cm. Those post-fix numbers are bit-identical to a control run in which the Control Rig node was STRUCTURALLY REMOVED from a throwaway duplicate ABP, which is what establishes that gating the node to Alpha 0 is equivalent to its absence rather than merely close to it.
roster_4up._scope_limit_foot_ik: CORRECTED - the previous text here said the foot-IK ControlRig 'cannot reach this rig', and that 'foot IK stays mannequin-only' named that absence rather than a preference. THAT WAS FALSE, and it was a 'rig X cannot do Y' claim inferred from a missing symbol rather than from a traced mechanism. The pass DID reach the MetaHuman; what it could not do was succeed. CR_Mannequin_FootIK solves foot_l/foot_r ONTO the ik_foot_l/ik_foot_r bone transforms (measured in-project in research/foot-ik-erratum.md with the trace off: it drives foot_l ONTO ik_foot_l, dL->0). Its Alpha was bound to GroundedFlag, which is 1 for the whole grounded take, so it ran at FULL WEIGHT on a skeleton that has no such bones; the effectors held a static transform and the solver planted the feet every frame while the correctly-remapped jog played above the pelvis. compare_skeletons puts 150 bone names in common with hierarchy_matches true and names what metahuman_base_skel does NOT have: weapon_l, weapon_r, ik_hand_root, ik_hand_gun, ik_hand_l, ik_hand_r, ik_foot_root, ik_foot_l, ik_foot_r, interaction, center_of_mass. The skeleton-aware Template turns that absence into an explicit gate instead of an accident: Alpha = GroundedFlag AND HasMannequinFootIKRig, the bool being GetBoneIndex('ik_foot_root') != -1 evaluated once at init.
roster_4up._what_the_shipped_frames_do_NOT_show: These frames DO evidence locomotion: all four rigs held the moving `Locomotion` state for 25 of 25 samples the render's OWN driver logged across the shipped range, and since the effector bake all four move their feet (see _which_rigs_actually_stride). What they are NOT: (a) evidence that Khaimera runs the same CLIPS as the mannequins - he runs baked retarget overrides (ABP_MT_Khaimera's CDO), and for this shot two of them are travel-pinned duplicates carrying the baked effector tracks; (b) evidence that foot IK is doing visible WORK on any rig - the pass is deliberately OFF on the MetaHuman, and on the mannequins and on Khaimera it RUNS but is near-identity on a flat floor, which is exactly what a correct effector track produces. The effector bake fixed a pass that was DESTROYING the stride; it did not add a visible foot-IK effect, and the shot is not offered as one. The pass IS shown doing real work on a ramp by Pie.FootIKNodeIntegration, not here; (c) evidence of root motion or of CharacterMovement - every capsule is held still with MOVE_None and the pose alone moves, which is what makes a fixed line-up legible; (d) A CLEAN FOOT PLANT ON ANY RIG. CORRECTED: the previous text here said Khaimera skates and that 'the mannequins do not slide - their source clips are authored in place'. THE SECOND HALF IS FALSE and was never measured. MF_Unarmed_Jog_Fwd is a TRAVELLING clip (its root translates 1060 cm over the loop) and this shot plays every rig on a MOVE_None capsule, so every planted foot treadmills. Measured off the clip data in root-locked space over the contact phase (planted = the lowest 25% of that foot's own Z range), horizontal speed of the planted foot: mannequin jog 437.1 / 412.0 cm/s, Khaimera's shipped in-place jog 514.2 / 455.0 cm/s, against a 600 cm/s drive speed. So ALL FOUR rigs slide, Khaimera by ~10-18% more than the mannequins rather than uniquely. Baking the effector tracks could not change this and was never going to: the effector carries the FK foot exactly, so the solve reproduces whatever slide the clip has - which is why the mannequins, whose effectors are genuinely authored, slide too. Removing it needs re-timed contacts or foot-lock IK, both larger changes than the bake. capture_check's motion test is likewise NOT evidence for this shot and is not offered as such: the camera move alone would satisfy it.
roster_4up._lineup_order: Left to right on camera: MetaHuman 158.371, Manny 180.544, Quinn 180.169, Khaimera 209.862 (boundsHeightUU, straight out of ScaleBaselines/*.json). That is ascending everywhere except the mannequin pair, which is inverted by 0.375 cm — 0.7% of the 51.5 cm spread. The per-rig figures this line-up was first laid out from ('Manny 180.2 / Quinn 180.5') are transposed relative to the committed baselines; the shipped order is the one those figures give, because reordering two rigs that differ by a third of a centimetre would invert the earlier three-rig take's order for a difference smaller than a pixel at this framing.
roster_4up._hand_r_z_range_three_figures_reconciled: Three different hand_r world-Z ranges for the MetaHuman appear across this line-up's record and a reader tracing 'the MetaHuman animates' hits all three with nothing saying how they relate. They are three DIFFERENT RUNS of the same probe, not three readings of one thing, and no caption cites any of them: 22.719 cm is the committed key below, from the first bind probe, and it is the only one this file asserts; 36.51 cm is quoted in _how_the_metahuman_bind_was_proven, from the post-fix probe run with the skeleton gate alongside foot_l 39.54 / foot_r 46.21, and its role there is to show hand_r 'essentially unchanged' by the skeleton gate - it is a BEFORE/AFTER pair with that run's own baseline, not with 22.719; 43.63 cm is from the hand-only probe run whose legs were FROZEN (foot_l 2.75 / foot_r 1.23), which is the reason the probe stopped sampling hand_r alone. Take-to-take spread on an arm swing is expected at this magnitude, and TWO things move between these runs, not one: the DRIVE SPEED changed - 22.719 was measured at Speed 450, while 43.63 and 36.51 were measured at Speed 600 (the probe switched to 600 because 600 IS the BlendSpace's jog sample rather than a 50/50 walk/jog blend, and it is the speed Pie.RigLocomotion characterises) - and the probe drives a fixed wall-clock window whose start is not phase-locked to the loop, so the range also depends on which part of the swing the window caught. An earlier version of this reconciliation attributed the whole spread to the window and stated Speed 600 for all three, which is wrong for the first. WHAT IS NOT TAKE-DEPENDENT is the verdict, which is why the probe's threshold is 0.5 cm and all three clear it by 45x or more. The figure that carries weight for 'the MetaHuman animates' is no longer a hand at all - it is foot_l/foot_r against a 10 cm floor fixed BEFORE the run, because the hand-only probe passed at 45x on a rig whose legs were frozen and whose arms swung.
roster_4up._how_the_jog_was_recovered_without_touch: The line-up first shipped STANDING because Khaimera's machine-local Khai_* clips carry their forward travel on the pelvis. Measured per key across all six clips before anything was authored: net pelvis-Y travel 1362.86 cm over the 1.767 s jog loop and 578.57 cm over the 1.5 s walk loop, while the ROOT track is identically zero (dx=dy=dz=0.00) in all six — so force_root_lock, which locks the root, had nothing to lock, and that route was not merely insufficient but inapplicable. The fix left every original byte-untouched and authored duplicates under /Game/MT/Khaimera/InPlace/ with the pelvis translation Y pinned to its first key. X sway (6.2 cm), Z bob (11.3 cm) and every rotation and scale key on every bone are unchanged: eight witness bones (foot_l, foot_r, calf_l, thigh_r, spine_01, hand_r, head, clavicle_l) re-sampled across EVERY key of original and duplicate agree to a max delta of 0.0. A linear de-ramp was measured and rejected — it leaves a 60.94 cm residual on the jog, and printed frame by frame that residual is one smooth bowl across the loop (the clip accelerates through its 1.767 s) rather than a per-stride surge, so it would have read as Khaimera sliding backwards and forwards once per loop against three neighbours that do not. Idle, Jump, Fall_Loop and Land were measured rather than assumed and need no treatment: net pelvis-Y travel 0.0 / 4.4 / 0.0 / 14.5 cm, and Jump's and Land's figures sit alongside 59.7 cm and 34.3 cm of pelvis Z, i.e. crouch-and-launch and absorb on one-shot clips that do not loop, not net travel.
roster_4up._in_frame_criterion: 'All four fully in frame for the whole shipped range' is tested, not eyeballed, and it is stated before the numbers. Geometric budget: the CineCamera at 32 mm on a 23.76 mm filmback covers ~809 cm at the ~1090 cm shooting distance against a 540 cm line-up, with the rigs 180 cm apart. That figure is context, not proof, and it is not even an upper bound: it is computed for a symmetric static camera while this camera dollies from y=-260 to y=+260 with the aim held at y=0. The direct frame measurement is the proof. The largest residual pelvis excursion of ANY rig in the shipped render is 18.0 cm (Khaimera 15.2, Manny 17.3, Quinn 17.8, MetaHuman 18.0 - from the render's own log): 10% of the inter-rig spacing, and mostly along each rig's own forward axis, which at this camera is DEPTH rather than screen-lateral. CORRECTED: an earlier version concluded here that 'neither edge is ever touched', which is more than its measurement supported. That detector was chroma-only, chosen because Khaimera is the only strongly chromatic subject - but the part of him that reaches the edge is a motion-blurred axe against black sky at RGB ~(47,47,46), CHROMA 1, invisible to a 'chroma never exceeds 8' test by construction. Re-measured on the shipped frames with Scripts/frame_edge_check.py (now committed, two independent channels, over the FULL height of each 30 px strip with nothing excluded), 60 frames sampled across [540,900): NO RIG BODY REACHES ANY EDGE - the rightmost chromatic body pixel is column 1873 of 1919, a 46 px margin - and the top strip is entirely clean at luma 0.0..0.9. Left and bottom carry only the anti-aliased horizon seam and floor texture, 0 of 60 frames above their own baseline. KHAIMERA'S AXE BLUR DOES CROSS THE RIGHT STRIP on 5 of the 60 sampled frames, reaching column 1919 of 1919, i.e. clipped by the frame edge. A blurred weapon grazing an edge is ordinary cinematography and no re-render was made for it; it is written down because the previous sentence denied it.
roster_4up._which_rigs_actually_stride: MEASURED PER RIG ON THE SHIPPED RANGE by the shipped render's OWN driver (scored from t >= 18.0 s, i.e. exactly frame_range [540,900]), world-Z range of each foot in cm, with the gate variable read back off each live AnimInstance: MetaHuman gate=false foot_l 35.68 foot_r 46.19; Manny gate=true 41.45 / 49.53; Quinn gate=true 41.41 / 49.53; Khaimera gate=true 64.94 / 75.55. ALL FOUR CLEAR THE FOOT-Z THRESHOLD against a 10 cm threshold fixed before the run from the mannequins' own measured swing. THE CONFOUND CONTROL IS THAT THREE OF THE FOUR DID NOT MOVE: Manny 41.45/49.53, Quinn 41.41/49.53 and the MetaHuman 35.68/46.19 are BIT-IDENTICAL to the previous take's shipped log (skeleton-aware Template, before the bake) on the same stage over the same window, so the only rig the effector bake changed is the one it was aimed at. Khaimera went 0.90 / 0.20 -> 64.94 / 75.55. WHY HE WAS PINNED, and it is not the MetaHuman's reason: he HAS ik_foot_root/l/r (198-bone Paragon skeleton), so the skeleton gate correctly read true and correctly left his foot-IK pass RUNNING - but all six of his baked retarget clips carry those tracks DEAD, at ik_foot_l translation spans of 0.000/0.000/0.000 against 14.163/116.384/50.635 on the mannequin source MF_Unarmed_Jog_Fwd. CR_Mannequin_FootIK solves the deform foot ONTO that bone, so A CONSTANT EFFECTOR PINS A FOOT EXACTLY AS A MISSING ONE DOES: bone presence is necessary but not sufficient. PROVEN BEFORE THE FIX, ASSET-FREE: forcing HasMannequinFootIKRig=false on his LIVE AnimInstance in PIE - no clip touched, the Control Rig pass simply bypassed - took his feet from 1.62 / 0.37 cm to 71.66 / 79.39 cm while the other three moved by the ordinary amount, which isolates the effector-consuming pass as the pinner. Real ik_foot_l/r tracks were then baked into the gitignored InPlace duplicates from his own FK feet.

roster_4up._effector_space_convention: MEASURED OFF THE WORKING MANNEQUIN CLIPS, NOT ASSUMED, and the relationship is EXACT. ik_foot_l's LOCAL transform (relative to its parent ik_foot_root) carries the FK foot's transform expressed in ik_foot_root space. Parent chains are identical on SK_Mannequin and Khaimera_Skeleton: ik_foot_l -> ik_foot_root -> root, and foot_l -> calf_l -> thigh_l -> pelvis -> root. Measured by MotionTerminal.Verify.IKEffectorDrives against the RAW animation data model, over every key of MF_Unarmed_Jog_Fwd and MF_Unarmed_Walk_Fwd, both feet, reproduced across two runs: rotation agrees to a max of 0.00103 deg and translation to a max of 0.0001 cm — one micron. The rival 'component space including the root bone' reading is excluded by orders of magnitude: under it the residual reaches -1059.86 cm by the end of the same clip. CORRECTED: this key previously reported a 'mirrored ~1.2 cm outboard offset, max 2.96 cm' and described Khaimera's bake as deliberately not reproducing it. There was no such offset and so no such choice. That figure came from a throwaway probe using AnimationLibrary.get_bone_pose_for_frame, which APPLIES the skeleton's bone translation retargeting mode; on SK_Mannequin the FK leg chain is AnimationScaled while the ik_foot_* chain is Animation, so the probe composed a SCALED chain and differenced it against an UNSCALED effector — translation only, rotation untouched, which is exactly why the rotation figures were right and the translation figures were not. On Khaimera_Skeleton every bone in both chains is Animation, which is why the bake and the test agree to 0.0000 cm there. The bake writes the exact FK foot transform, making the solve an identity on the deform foot so the authored stride survives the pass intact.

_planted_phase_slide_cm_s._method: From CLIP DATA, not PIE sampling. A first attempt sampled a slate pre-tick callback and got 28 ticks over 9 s (~3 Hz); slide is a per-frame velocity, so at 0.33 s between samples a foot moves through most of a stride between consecutive 'planted' reads and the resulting 296 cm/s was aliasing. Discarded. Every rig here is driven with MOVE_None so the SOURCE foot path is the clip's path in root-locked space. CORRECTED: these are clip-data speeds, not measurements of the shipped pixels. The evaluated pose is additionally rotated by the aim-offset defect downstream of the clip, so the ON-SCREEN foot path is NOT identical to this and was never measured, which is the foot expressed in ik_foot_root space - the same quantity the effector bake writes. PLANTED = the lowest 25% of that foot's own Z range over the loop, per foot, so the band scales with the rig.
_planted_phase_slide_cm_s._comparator: THE EXPECTED VALUE FOR A PLANTED FOOT ON THIS STAGE IS 0 cm/s, not 600. Every capsule is MOVE_None, so a foot in contact with the ground should be motionless in world space; any non-zero number here is slide. The 600 cm/s figure is the GAIT SPEED the clips were authored to travel at and is quoted only to show that the slide is of the same order as the travel the in-place conversion removed — it is the cause, not the pass mark. Measured against the correct comparator of 0, the mannequins slide 437.1 / 412.0 cm/s and Khaimera 514.2 / 455.0 cm/s: nobody plants.

roster_4up._effector_drift_measurement_source: MotionTerminal.Verify.IKEffectorDrives, which reads the RAW animation data model — the authoritative read for an authored-data question. Do NOT re-derive these from AnimationLibrary.get_bone_pose_for_frame: that API answers 'what will evaluation produce', applying bone translation retargeting, which is a different question and gave a wrong answer once already.
